knowledge:
- key_parameters: reads=GRanges object containing aligned reads ;; zeta=segmentation parameter representing nucleosome length (typically 147) ;; delta=segmentation parameter (e.g., 40 or 50) ;; maxLength=maximum length of a segment (larger segments require more iterations to reach convergence) ;; nbrIterations=number of MCMC iterations (e.g., 100000 for testing, 1000000+ recommended for real data) ;; lambda=prior parameter for the number of nucleosomes ;; kMax=maximum number of nucleosomes in a segment ;; minInterval/maxInterval=minimum and maximum distance between nucleosomes ;; minReads=minimum number of reads in a segment to run RJMCMC ;; extendingSize=parameter for postTreatment (should be kept below 20 to avoid merging true nucleosomes) ;; nbCores=number of cores for parallel execution in rjmcmcCHR
- alternatives: Frequentist inferences within parametric approaches (e.g., hidden Markov models with assumed known order) or modified Gaussian mixture models (e.g., NOrMAL).
- when_to_use: When profiling nucleosome positions from high-throughput short-read data (MNase-Seq) and a fully Bayesian hierarchical model is desired to estimate both the positions and the number of nucleosomes simultaneously.
- pitfalls: The rjmcmc function can only analyze one chromosome at a time; each chromosome must be analyzed separately. Do not merge segments from different chromosomes together. The RJMCMC method tends to over-split read distributions for a single nucleosome (increasing false positives); therefore, postTreatment must be run on the entire merged region (not on individual segments) to merge closely positioned nucleosomes. Setting extendingSize too high (above 20) in postTreatment can cause the merging of true nucleosomes.

workflows.name: segmented_nucleosome_positioning
workflows.intent: Segment a genomic region, run RJMCMC on individual segments, merge the results, post-process to reduce false positives, and visualize predicted nucleosomes.
input: sample$dataIP (data frame containing chromosome, start, end, and strand of aligned short reads)
workflows.stages: 1. Segment the analyzed region into candidate regions using segmentation ;; 2. Run RJMCMC on individual segments using rjmcmc ;; 3. Merge predicted nucleosomes from all segments using mergeAllRDSFilesFromDirectory ;; 4. Post-process predictions on the merged region using postTreatment ;; 5. Visualize predicted nucleosomes using plotNucleosomes
workflows.code:
library(GenomicRanges)

## Transform sample dataset into GRanges object
sampleGRanges <- GRanges(seqnames = sample$dataIP$chr, 
                        ranges = IRanges(start = sample$dataIP$start, 
                                        end = sample$dataIP$end), 
                        strand = sample$dataIP$strand)

## Segment sample into candidate regions
sampleSegmented <- segmentation(reads = sampleGRanges, zeta = 147, 
                                delta = 40, maxLength = 1000)

## Number of segments created
length(sampleSegmented)

## Extract the first segment 
segment01 <- sampleSegmented[[1]]

## Run RJMCMC analysis
## A higher number of iterations is recommanded for real analysis
resultSegment01 <- rjmcmc(reads  = segment01, nbrIterations = 100000, 
                            lambda = 3, kMax = 30,
                            minInterval = 100, maxInterval = 200, 
                            minReads = 5, vSeed = 1921)

## Print the predicted nucleosomes for the first segment
resultSegment01

## The directory containing the results of all segments
## On RDS file has been created for each segment
directory <- system.file("extdata", "demo_vignette", 
                            package = "RJMCMCNucleosomes")

## Merging predicted nucleosomes from all segments
resultsAllMerged <- mergeAllRDSFilesFromDirectory(directory)

resultsAllMerged

## Split reads from the initial sample data into forward and reverse subsets
reads <- GRanges(sample$dataIP)

## Number of nucleosomes before the post-treatment
resultsAllMerged$k

## Use the post-treatment function
resultsPostTreatment <- postTreatment(reads = reads,
                            resultRJMCMC = resultsAllMerged,
                            extendingSize = 15,
                            chrLength = max(start(reads), end(reads)) + 1000)

## Number of nucleosomes after the post-treatment
length(resultsPostTreatment)

## Extract reads to create a GRanges
reads <-GRanges(sample$dataIP)

## Merge predictions from before post-treatment and after post-treatment in 
## a list so that both results will be shown in graph
# resultsBeforeAndAfter <- list(Sample = c(sample$wp$nucleopos,
#                                             sample$fuz$nucleopos),
#                                BeforePostTreatment = resultsAllMerged$mu,
#                                AfterPostTreatment = resultsPostTreatment)
resultsBeforeAndAfter <- GRangesList(Sample = GRanges(
        rep("chr_SYNTHETIC", 
            length(c(sample$wp$nucleopos,sample$fuz$nucleopos))), 
        ranges = IRanges(start=c(sample$wp$nucleopos,sample$fuz$nucleopos),
                        end=c(sample$wp$nucleopos,sample$fuz$nucleopos)), 
        strand=rep("*", length(c(sample$wp$nucleopos,
                                sample$fuz$nucleopos)))),
                        BeforePostTreatment = resultsAllMerged$mu,
                        AfterPostTreatment = resultsPostTreatment)
## Create graph using nucleosome positions and reads
## The plot will shows : 
## 1. nucleosomes from the sample
## 2. nucleosomes detected by rjmcmc() function
## 3. nucleosomes obtained after post-treament 
plotNucleosomes(nucleosomePositions = resultsBeforeAndAfter, reads = reads, 
                    names=c("Sample", "RJMCMC", "After Post-Treatment"))

workflows.name: chromosomal_nucleosome_positioning
workflows.intent: Run the entire nucleosome positioning pipeline (segmentation, RJMCMC, merging, and post-processing) on a single chromosome in one step.
input: syntheticNucleosomeReads$dataIP (data frame containing chromosome, start, end, and strand of aligned short reads)
workflows.stages: 1. Run rjmcmcCHR on the chromosome GRanges object to automatically segment, run RJMCMC, merge, and post-process.
workflows.code:
## Use the dataset to create a GRanges object
sampleGRanges <- GRanges(syntheticNucleosomeReads$dataIP)

## All reads are related to one chromosome called "chr_SYNTHETIC"
seqnames(sampleGRanges)

## Run RJMCMC on all reads
result <- rjmcmcCHR(reads = sampleGRanges,
                seqName = "chr_SYNTHETIC", dirOut = "testRJMCMCCHR",
                zeta = 147, delta=50, maxLength=1200,
                nbrIterations = 500, lambda = 3, kMax = 30,
                minInterval = 146, maxInterval = 292, minReads = 5,
                vSeed = 10113, nbCores = 2, saveAsRDS = FALSE,
                saveSEG = FALSE)

result
